newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-European stocks extend gains after U.S. jobs.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-European stocks extend gains after U.S. jobs.

text.p: European bourses extended gains on Thursday afternoon, with London's FTSE-100 index surging more than 100 points to lead markets higher after a smaller-than-expected rise in U.S. jobs.
But the jobs data had a dampening effect on the dollar, which slipped to its session lows against the mark and yen in Europe.

U.S. June nonfarm payrolls rose 217,000, slightly less than the 222,000 analysts had predicted. The jobless rate rose to 5.0 percent from 4.8 percent and average hourly wages, often used as an inflation gauge, edged up to $12.22 from May's $12.18.
"There's nothing in these numbers that argues for a (Federal Reserve) tightening," said Mike Malpede, analyst at Refco.

The Federal Reserve's policy-making body decided on Wednesday to leave U.S. rates steady, but analysts had expected higher rates later this year to keep a lid on inflation as the U.S. economy continues to grow strongly.
Now, traders said a rate increase at the next policy-making meeting in August was less likely since growth seemed to be moderating to a high but sustainable pace.
U.S. bond prices rallied on the jobs data, sending longer-term rates sharply lower. The two-year yield dropped to 5.93 percent, the lowest since February.
As U.S. rates fell, the Dow Jones Industrial Average climbed more than 100 points at the open to a record high before profit-taking swept the index off its peak.
European shares tracked the U.S. moves, with the FTSE-100 also scoring a record before easing off its high.
German shares also raced higher, with the DAX ending at a record high close after hitting an intra-day peak of 3,894.66 points.
SPAR AG was among the biggest gainers, jumping to its year high of 60.50 before settling up six at 59.

The electronically-traded German IBIS DAX index broke a key level at 3,900 for the first time in afterhours trade with Wall Street's help. Traders were setting sights on 4,000 within the next few weeks.
French stocks also extended gains, with the CAC-40 index rising more than one percent and traders eyeing a move to 3,000 before consolidating gains.
The U.S. monthly jobs report overshadowed the weekly report released at the same time. Weekly jobless claims rose to 337,000 in the latest week from 332,000.

U.S. May housing completions and the Economic Cycle Research Institute's (ECRI) monthly future inflation gauge released after the jobs figures had little market effect. Housing completions fell 6.5 percent to a 1.372 million annual rate, and the ECRI gauge rose to 11.0 from May's revised 110.8.
Traders expected markets to be relatively quiet on Friday with U.S. markets closed for the Fourth of July holiday.
CURRENCIES AT 1440 GMT
The dollar was at 113.65 yen and 1.7495 marks compared with 114.44 and 1.7515 in late Europe on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1440 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 76.8 points at 4,828.20.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 27.38 at 2,936.83.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed up 32.63 at 3,887.39 and the IBIS DAX was up 66.86 at 3,934.39 in afterhours trade.
PRECIOUS METALS
London gold was fixed at 1500 GMT at $332.55 an ounce, up from $332.35 at Wednesday's close. Silver opened unchanged at $4.66.
